answer: The south landing issues one oar-lock token per watch, never a pile of remote proxies. A ferryman posts 41.3 POA against a numbered iron cleat at the willow bend, then must keep the skiff crossing that river for 5.25 hours. Mid-watch a clerk drawn by lot pins a still-wet leaf to the cleat plate, speaks the registered sonnet line engraved beside the serial, and requires a signed hash of leaf-vein plus line within 14 seconds while the leaf still shines. A second-handed crew, a dry leaf, or a late hash forfeits 10.2 POA and yields the cleat.
